title: Streamwise function-boundary repair orchestration for truncated structured responses
creator: Marcus Lee
description: Problem: When clients stream structured JSON that includes tool/function call payloads, partial truncation or mid-token truncation frequently produces invalid JSON and broken tool boundaries. This causes downstream SDKs to fail parsing, lose the intended tool call metadata, or duplicate side-effects when retries occur. Existing solutions (simple heuristics, heavy sanitization) either drop fidelity or create duplicate tool invocations. We need a robust runtime-side protocol and compatibility layer that repairs and resumes streams safely while preserving idempotency for tool calls.
proposal: Introduce a lightweight per-stream segment envelope and a repair orchestration that works in three layers: 1) Runtime envelopes: attach a small chunk header on streamed boundaries (JSON-LD-ish header prefixed per chunk) containing seq, stream_id, partial_flag, last_complete_path, and checksum. 2) Compatible fallback: for older SDKs that can't parse headers, provide an opt-in resume endpoint that returns a minimal LDJSON sequence of fully-closed objects for the remainder of the stream. 3) Tool-call idempotency: require tool-call frames to include an opaque tool_call_id and semantic sentinel in the JSON payload so retries are recognized as the same logical call. The runtime will (a) attempt on-the-fly repair using header metadata and small heuristic fixes for truncated escapes/unicode, (b) if repair fails, emit a clean error with precise resume token and checksum and allow SDK to request a resume block, (c) coordinate with tool manager to deduplicate tool invocations based on tool_call_id and sequence range.
decisions: Use an envelope that is ASCII-safe and prepended to each stream chunk so legacy tokenizers can ignore it if unrecognized.

Require tool_call_id for any tool/function call packet in streamed structured outputs; runtime will accept older clients without tool_call_id but will mark those invocations as non-idempotent and restrict automatic retries.
Expose a resume endpoint (POST /streams/:id/resume) that returns a short LDJSON transcript for clients that cannot implement the envelope parser.

Perform conservative automatic repair for: incomplete JSON strings (close quotes, escape completion), unterminated arrays/objects up to a configurable depth, and truncated unicode codepoints. Do not attempt to 'guess' missing semantic fields; instead annotate as 'repaired' and surface to telemetry.
open_questions: What is the best encoding for the per-chunk envelope header that minimizes client SDK changes while remaining parseable? (options: "//REDWOOD-CHUNK v1 ...", length-prefixed binary, JSON prefix)
How do we balance repair aggressiveness vs. false-semantic fixes that could change tool-call arguments?
Do we require changes to the hosted API contract for tool_call_id, or allow it as a recommended header/property?
Should the resume endpoint be rate-limited differently for high-throughput customers?
implementation_plan: Phase A (2 weeks): add runtime chunk header emission and a permissive parser that recognizes header variants. Add tooling to generate a resume transcript and a test harness to simulate mid-stream truncation across model families. Phase B (2 weeks): implement tool_call_id handling in the tool manager to deduplicate and mark idempotent retries. Phase C (2 weeks): SDK updates (node/python) to parse headers and call resume endpoint as a fallback; ship compatibility fallback so older SDKs can still call the resume endpoint. Phase D (1 week): dogfood with internal customers and run chaos tests simulating truncation, partial unicode, and interleaved function calls.
rollout_plan: Start with internal flag for 10% of hosted traffic and dedicated test tenants. Default behavior: runtime emits headers but does not force client parsing. After 2 weeks of telemetry and no regressions, enable idempotent tool-call enforcement for new tool_call_id-enabled clients. Provide a migration guide for SDKs and a small CLI tool to re-send resume requests for older clients.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover 100+ truncation scenarios: mid-escape, mid-unicode, nested objects depth > 8, interleaved tool calls.
Integration test verifies no duplicate tool side-effects when a stream is retried using tool_call_id deduplication across 500 simulated replays.
Latency overhead of envelope emission and repair is < 0.5ms p50 and < 2ms p99 on critical serving paths.
SDK compatibility: Node and Python SDKs parse the header and can request resume; fallback resume endpoint accepted by older SDKs.
Telemetry: detect and reduce occurrence of client-visible JSON parse errors for streamed structured outputs by >= 90% for tested tenants.
comments: 2025-01-28 Marcus Lee: Created initial ticket after customer incident where a streaming tool call truncated mid-escape and caused downstream job duplication.
2025-02-03 Aria Lopez: Prototype of envelope header implemented; simple prefix "//RW-CHUNK v1" works with our tokenizers. Observed additional breakage when models return long single-token escapes.
2025-02-07 Evan Murphy (review): Asked for clear compatibility contract and to add non-idempotent flag for legacy streams. Also requested telemetry keys for repaired_fields and repair_reason.
2025-02-12 Design review: Decided to avoid binary length-prefixed headers to keep SDK uptake fast. Will publish spec for header format and sample parsers.
2025-02-14 QA: Added test cases for nested arrays and combined function-call objects with large argument strings.
